title: Mr. Stacks warns Adams's family of a white mob
summary: Neighbor Stacks warns that hoodlums will attack colored families and offers his bed; Adams's father refuses to leave his house.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Oh yeah, then the other white people began then to all around the house, they said we were going to kill up a lot of colored folks on the ground. That riot, you see, was the police on them. And doing that to Mr. Stacks, the same boy, I tell you I know this one, probably his dad. He lived next door to us. Come and warn my dad and told him that some hoodlums going to form up a gang and come all around and kill all the colored folks. On account of that riot. We didn't know nothing about them. We were way out in front of that. We were way back in town here. We were nowhere around. We didn't know nothing about them. We don't know what we heard. Yeah. We were way out of that. And so, anyway, Mr. Stacks come and notified my dad and asked him, say, no, I don't trust him. Listen, I told my wife who got to bed, say, you and your madam are going to sleep in my bed. That's where me and my madam sleep in. And Frank, that's me, and my other brother next to me was in Chicago now, my younger brother, I'm going to sleep in the bed with Walter and Eddie. Eddie's up there, but Walter died. He said, I was the younger brother, died. Only Eddie's living. And so, I told my dad, and so my dad, he said, no. He says, uh, I said, Stacks, I thank you ever so much. But he says, no, he says, I'd be less than a man who leave my house to go in your house. He said, you know, I don't bother nobody. I never did. He said, no, I know you didn't. He said, but Adam, you going to stay around there? He says, I'm going to walk the street all night long with his shotgun. He said, and he going to tell them, none of them stop in this block to harm any one of you couples. The dude is going to have to kill me all my day. At least he'll have to die. Because he ain't going to take back and say he's going to kill him. And then he'll have to kill him. And he said, he'd rather die right there until he's going to fight for him. He ain't going to let nobody stop in that block to battle those kind of people at all.
He's a good friend of yours. Oh yeah.
Nice friend. So then my daddy, he asked my daddy, he said, well, what you going to do about it? Hold just a second.
Hold just a second. Here we go.
We'll have another chair, Bill. All right.
